subject: Derivative provenance, residency and subprocessor evidence — next steps
messages:
From: Elena Mendez <elena.mendez@healthsol.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 13:12:00 +0100
Subject: Derivative rights, residency and subprocessors — HealthSol questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — HealthSol's legal/privacy team has a short set of follow-up questions so we can proceed with a pilot. I've attached our DPA-focused questionnaire and a redline with suggested clauses. High-level asks:

- Can Redwood commit to "no model training" on HealthSol tenant data (no adaptive training, no model weights updates) and include that in the DPA? We need clear language and an operational definition.
- If a no-training commitment isn't feasible for hosted customers by default, what evidence can you provide that data processed for inference is not used to improve models (logs, retention windows, config flags, attestation)?
- Residency: for EU patient data we need processing to remain within EU regions and for key material to be EU-resident (KMS). What options do you offer?
- Subprocessors: please share current subprocessor list and whether any subprocessor has cross-border transfer rights.
- Proof: we'll need an evidence bundle (kinds of logs, sample export, attestation) to present to our InfoSec. Can you give an estimated timeline for that?

Attachments: HealthSol_DPA_questions.pdf, redline_dpa_v1.pdf

Appreciate a short call to align on the deliverables and timeline.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Mendez
Senior Privacy Counsel | HealthSol Inc.
email: elena.mendez@healthsol.com
phone: +44 20 7946 0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Mendez <elena.mendez@healthsol.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 15:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Derivative rights, residency and subprocessors — HealthSol questions

Hi Elena — thanks for sending these over and for the redline. We're aligned that this is an important gating item for the pilot. Summary of what Redwood can commit and next steps below; technical/ops detail from David follows in a separate email.

Quick answers (high level):
- No-training commitment: Redwood can include a clear no-model-training clause for tenant data in the DPA for hosted EU pilots. By default our hosted customers are not used for model training without explicit opt-in, but we will put the commitment in writing (verbiage suggestion: "Redwood will not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or improve foundation models or model weights unless Customer provides explicit written consent").
- Operational evidence: we can provide an evidence bundle that includes process notes, configuration flags (no-learning toggles), a short export of anonymized metadata showing retention windows, and a signed attestation from our privacy team.
- Residency: options are (1) EU-hosted tenancy with EU-only routing + EU KMS, (2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) in an EU region, or (3) Private VPC deployment / on-prem for strict isolates. We'll outline trade-offs and costs.
- Subprocessors: we'll provide the current subprocessor roster and mark any that transfer data outside the EU; we can also discuss contractual flow-downs.

Suggested next steps / timeline:
1) Quick 30-min call this week to confirm scope and which evidence items HealthSol needs (logs, samples, attestation).
2) We produce a tentative evidence bundle within 5 business days after the call.
3) Legal to exchange a DPA redline incorporating the no-training clause; Redwood can offer a one-time executive attestation within 7 business days of DPA signature for the pilot period.

I've attached our ops evidence checklist to show typical items we supply. If that looks good, let's schedule a call.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0173

Attachments: redwood_ops_evidence_checklist.xlsx

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Mendez <elena.mendez@healthsol.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:32:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Derivative rights, residency and subprocessors — HealthSol questions

Hi all — adding a few concrete details from the infra/ops side so HealthSol can validate requirements against your checklist:

- No-training flagging: requests for inference can be tagged at the tenant or API-key level. By default the "learner_enabled" flag is false for our hosted EU tenants. We can produce a small configuration snapshot showing the flag state for the pilot tenant.
- KV / caching: transient KV cache is used for request-level latency; we can guarantee ephemeral KV lifetime and show retention configs. We do not checkpoint tenant interaction into any persistent training corpus unless explicitly scheduled for a named fine-tune job.
- Logs & telemetry: we can provide audit logs that show request timestamps, tenant id, and routing decisions. For privacy reasons we will provide an anonymized sample export (no PII) that demonstrates retention and routing.
- KMS & keys: EU KMS options are available; we can either bring-your-own-key or use our EU KMS instance. For on-prem / private deployments, keys are customer-controlled.
- Subprocessors & transfers: current subprocessors are listed in our SCC-compliant roster; any cross-border subprocessors are highlighted. We will note role (hosting, CDN, logging) and whether they have potential to access plaintext.

Operational timeline (estimates):
- Call to scope: 2-3 days to book
- Evidence bundle (initial): 3-5 business days after scope confirmed
- Attestation (signed): 5-7 business days after evidence reviewed

Open questions for HealthSol:
1) For the attestation, do you need a signed letter on company letterhead or is a Jira/DocuSign workflow acceptable?
2) Do you require sampling of actual API traffic logs or is an anonymized synthetic sample sufficient for your InfoSec?

If you confirm, we'll start preparing artifacts and coordinate with legal for the DPA redline.

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Director, Platform Privacy | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Mendez <elena.mendez@healthsol.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Derivative rights, residency and subprocessors — HealthSol questions

Marissa / David — thanks, this is helpful and addresses most of our checklist. Quick answers:

- Attestation: we prefer a signed letter on Redwood letterhead (DocuSign OK).
- Sample logs: anonymized synthetic sample is acceptable for the initial review; InfoSec may request a narrow real sample under an NDA later.

Let's do the 30-min call on Thursday (local time) — my calendar is open 09:00–12:00 BST. On the call we'll confirm which evidence items to include in the first bundle and agree a timeline for the DPA redline.

Thanks — attaching our availability and a short note on the legal points we will insist on in the pilot DPA.

Best,
Elena
Senior Privacy Counsel | HealthSol Inc.
